newsitem.title: UK: MOTOR RACING-LOLA FORCED TO PULL OUT OF F1 SEASON.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-LOLA FORCED TO PULL OUT OF F1 SEASON.

text.p: The Lola Formula One motor racing team confirmed their immediate withdrawal from this year's world championship on Wednesday.
The British-based team, who entered the season with high hopes, were forced to pull out because of financial problems associated with one of their sponsors.

"It was a timetable situation really," said a team source. "In our case we needed the money up front because that is where the investment is needed. The balance of finance as it stood was not favourable.

"...We tried to get alternative funds arranged, including additional sponsors, but we were late in starting this programme, we were late in getting the cars ready and we have been late in getting on to them.
"I won't say that Lola will not return to grand prix racing in the future because Formula One is the pinnacle of the sport and we have vowed to participate in it."

Neither of the team's two cars, driven by Italian Vincenzo Sospiri and Brazilian Ricardo Rosset, qualified for the Australian Grand Prix in Melbourne three weeks ago and it was likely that scenario would have been repeated at this weekend's Brazilian Grand Prix in Interlagos.

On Wednesday morning, a team spokesman revealed that they would be pulling out of the Brazilian race because of "technical and financial problems" before the decision was made later in the day to pull out completely.
Team founder Eric Broadley has enjoyed wide success in his three decades in the sport.
He formed Lola Cars Ltd in 1958, supplying chassis to a number of teams before seeing a Lola-Honda driven by John Surtees win the 1967 Italian Grand Prix at Monza.
More recently, his company have enjoyed similar triumphs in the American IndyCar series, where it helped former world champion Briton Nigel Mansell win the 1994 title.
Broadley's decision to enter grand prix racing with his own out-and-out team was only made last November after their most recent association with Scuderia Italia in 1993 proved disastrous.
Despite the lateness of the move, he had high hopes for success this season.

"The company is ready for this," he said at the launch of the Ford-powered T97/30 in London last month. "And I would hope by the end of four years we will be ready to win the championship. We are not expecting massive results this year -- we have a lot to learn about Formula One."
